title: Operational Regime Selection
purpose: Define operational regime selection as a deterministic RT classification process rather than a static property.

motivation.problem: The framework now has derived L, NL, boundary, and mixed regime classifications, but the selection step that chooses among them is still implicit.
motivation.resolution: Operational regime selection is governed as a deterministic RT classification process driven by orientation, admissibility, residue, and declared context under RT_core.

core_definition.regime_selection: Operational regime classification is produced by evaluating orientation together with admissibility and residue under RT_core.
core_definition.trace_requirement: Every selected regime must constructively trace to RT_core.

governance_rules.name: Selection Not Assumption
governance_rules.statement: Operational regimes are selected, not assumed.

governance_rules.name: Reproducible Selection
governance_rules.statement: Selection must be reproducible from the declared inputs.

governance_rules.name: Traceable Classification
governance_rules.statement: Every regime classification must be traceable.

effects: Registers operational regime selection as a governed RT classification process.
Keeps the selection step dynamic and repeatable without altering RT_core.
Allows Linear, Nonlinear, and Mixed outputs to be selected from declared inputs.

notes: Existing RT, L, NL, boundary, and mixed definitions remain canonical.
Selection only determines which classification applies from the declared inputs.
Mixed output remains governed by the explicit separation conditions already defined in PATCH_PI_RT_CALCULUS_007.
Operational regime selection is a deterministic classification process, not a static property.
Mixed output remains contingent on the explicit separation basis already introduced for mixed L/NL regimes.
This patch is governance and architecture only.
Selection classifies regimes under RT_core and does not modify the canonical root expression.
